# Monthly Sales Dashboard Plan

A clean 3-chart dashboard will show growth over time, category mix, and the discount-to-margin tradeoff. The dataset is small, so the best layout is a compact executive view with clear filters and a short insights panel.

## Dashboard Layout and Chart Design

### 1) Revenue Trend by Month
- **Chart type:** Line chart
- **X-axis:** Month
- **Y-axis:** Revenue
- **Series:** Total monthly revenue
- **Purpose:** Show overall sales momentum and month-to-month growth

### 2) Revenue by Product Category
- **Chart type:** Stacked bar chart
- **X-axis:** Month
- **Y-axis:** Revenue
- **Stack segments:** Electronics, Furniture
- **Purpose:** Show how each category contributes to total revenue each month

### 3) Discount Rate vs Profit Margin
- **Chart type:** Scatter plot
- **X-axis:** Discount rate
- **Y-axis:** Profit margin
- **Points:** One point per month-category record
- **Color:** Category
- **Purpose:** Reveal whether higher discounts are associated with lower margins

## Recommended Data Prep

| Step | What to do | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Aggregate monthly revenue | Sum revenue across categories by month | 4 monthly totals |
| Split by category | Keep revenue by month and category | Stacked bar-ready series |
| Preserve row-level records | Use each month-category row as one scatter point | 8 scatter points |
| Add labels/tooltips | Show month, category, revenue, discount, margin | Better drill-down |

## Key Metrics to Display

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total revenue | **$963,000** |
| Highest month | **2024-04: $239,000** |
| Strongest category | **Electronics** in every month |
| Highest profit margin | **0.27** |
| Lowest profit margin | **0.14** |

## Three Insights

- **Revenue is steadily rising** from **$200,000 in January** to **$239,000 in April**, which suggests consistent demand growth.
- **Electronics drives most of the revenue** each month, contributing more than Furniture in every period.
- **Higher discounts generally align with lower profit margins**, especially visible in Furniture, where discount rates are higher and margins are weaker.

## Anomalies and Watchouts

- **Furniture in March** stands out: discount rate jumps to **0.15** while profit margin drops to **0.14**, the weakest margin in the dataset.
- **Electronics remains resilient**: even as discount rates decline from **0.08 to 0.05**, profit margin improves from **0.22 to 0.27**.
- **Revenue growth is not equally efficient across categories**: Furniture revenue improves at a slower pace than Electronics and appears more sensitive to discounting.

## Quick Actions

- Chart.js documentation: https://www.chartjs.org/docs/latest/

- Tableau visualization guide: https://www.tableau.com/learn/articles/data-visualization
